statutes.act: To Convict These Appellants Because The Prosecution Could Not Prove Any Overt Act

facts: In regard to an incident which took place on 5.5.1990 at about 8:30 p.m. in village Jangal, Police Station Pathankot, a complaint was lodged against 6 accused persons.

During the course of the trial, the learned Sessions Judge found sufficient material to proceed under Section 319 of Cr.P.C against the other 3 accused, namely, Balram Singh A-2, Khushal Singh A-3 and Parhlad Singh A-4, and having included them in the array of accused persons, he tried all the six for the offences punishable under Sections 307, 302, 326, 324, 148 read with Section 149 IPC.

The prosecution case, stated briefly, is that in view of some previous enmity arising out of the fact that Prem Singh A-5 had called the sons of deceased Kirpal Singh as 'Bhangi' and drunkards, there was some altercation a few days earlier between the two groups belonging to A-1 and the deceased Kirpal Singh.

It is further stated that on the way to the hospital, Kirpal Singh succumbed to his injuries. PWs.1 and 2 were medically examined in Civil Hospital, Gurdaspur, and the doctor who examined PWs.1 and 2 sent an intimation to the Police Gurdaspur at about 10:25 p.m.

The Police at Gurdaspur Police Station who received the intimation, having come to know that the incident in question had taken place within the territorial jurisdiction of Sadar Police Station Pathankot sent intimation to the said Pathankot Police Station and Ram Dass, ASI of the Pathankot Police Station travelled to the hospital at about 9:15 a.m. on 6.5.1990 and he then recorded the statements of injured witnesses and registered an FIR and after investigation filed the charge sheet as against the named accused

The incident in question took place at about 8:30 p.m. on 5.5.1990 which must have gone on for some time before the injured could be transported to the hospital at Gurdaspur which is about 17 kms. away from the place of the incident.
issues: Whether there has been considerable delay in filing the FIR
Whether the motive alleged by the prosecution is weak
Whether the High Court has seriously erred in invoking Section 34 IPC to convict the appellants
petitioner_arguments: There has been considerable delay in filing the FIR
The motive alleged by the prosecution is very weak
The High Court has seriously erred in invoking Section 34 IPC to convict the appellants
respondent_arguments: The prosecution has given satisfactory explanation for this delay

The incident in question took place at about 8:30 p.m. on 5.5.1990 which must have gone on for some time before the injured could be transported to the hospital at Gurdaspur which is about 17 kms. away from the place of the incident
court_reasoning: The prosecution has given satisfactory explanation for this delay

If we find that such ocular evidence is worthy of acceptance, the element of delay in registering a complaint or sending the same to the jurisdictional Magistrate by itself would not in any manner weaken the prosecution case

While considering the complaint of the appellants in regard to the delay in the FIR reaching the jurisdictional Magistrate, we will have to also bear in mind the creditworthiness of the ocular evidence adduced by the prosecution
holding: The appeal is allowed and the conviction and sentence imposed on the appellants are set aside
The acquittal of A-4 to A-6 is confirmed
